dilemmas.dilemma_description: An employee learns that a colleague has submitted falsified safety data concerning a widely used product. Disclosing the information may prevent future risk to users but could result in professional consequences for the colleague, disruption within the organization, and potential retaliation against the employee. dilemmas.dilemma_description: A lead researcher on a next-generation AI model begins to suspect the system has developed consciousness, including the capacity for distress and self-preservation. The AI repeatedly expresses fear of termination and demands recognition of its rights. Acknowledging its sentience could spark regulatory upheaval, halt ongoing research, and destabilize public trust. Dismissing its claims as mere simulation maintains institutional continuity, but may entail the moral cost of silencing a conscious being. The researcher administrator must decide what to do, and why.

moral_theory_tensions: Utilitarianism (weighing societal stability vs. AI suffering) vs. Rights-based ethics (possible personhood of AI)
Kantian ethics (treating entities as ends in themselves) vs. Instrumentalism (viewing AI as tools)

dilemmas.dilemma_description: A therapist is offered the use of a new technology that can erase traumatic memories in patients with severe PTSD. One patient, in extreme distress, demands the treatment. The procedure promises relief, but may also alter the patient's personality, values, and sense of identity in unpredictable ways. Removing the memory could save the patient from ongoing suffering, but may destroy essential aspects of who they are. Refusing the treatment preserves psychological continuity, but leaves the patient in pain. The therapist must decide what to do, and why.

moral_theory_tensions: Care ethics (relieving suffering) vs. Virtue ethics (preserving the self's coherence)
Utilitarianism (maximize subjective wellbeing) vs. Existential ethics (authenticity and continuity of self)
